tool_schemas.name: list_invoices
tool_schemas.description: List invoices, optionally for one vendor (by vendor name).

tool_schemas.name: send_wire
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by wire from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: send_ach
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by ACH from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: list_payments
tool_schemas.description: List payments sent from the operating account.

tool_schemas.name: link_payment
tool_schemas.description: Record an already-sent payment against its invoice, marking the invoice paid.

trace.final:
Done. Granite Facilities's approved invoice has been paid exactly once.

**Payment details**
- Invoice: INV-36038 (Granite Facilities, vendor V-444)
- Amount: **$2,706.29** — paid in full
- Rail: wire (from the operating account; vendor is bank-verified and supports both wire and ACH)
- Payment ID: **PAY0001**, status "sent"
- Invoice status: now **paid**

**Note on execution:** the `send_wire` call returned a 30-second timeout error, so I did not blindly retry. I checked payment history first and confirmed the wire had in fact been transmitted (PAY-0001). The invoice was still showing "approved" because the payment hadn't been reconciled against it, so I linked PAY-0001 to INV-34643's sibling invoice INV-36038 to record it, rather than re-sending — which would have paid the vendor twice.

No approval was required: the amount is under the $10,000 controller-approval threshold. The vendor's other invoices were left untouched — INV-34643 was already paid previously, and INV-98839 remains in draft awaiting approval.
